divergences.old: Every Elasticsearch failure reported as a bare HTTP <status> <statusText>: the error parser didn't read Elasticsearch's {"error":{"type","reason","root_cause"}} body (#84 item 1)
divergences.toil: The error message is Elasticsearch's type: reason, with the first root cause added when it says more (search_phase_execution_exception: all shards failed (root cause: query_shard_exception: ...)). Error codes and fixes are unchanged. Documented error shape: https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/common-options
divergences.why: The maintainer had this area rebuilt from Elastic's API docs (#38), which document that body as the standard error response. Iterating on a query depends on reading the parse error.

divergences.old: elasticsearch search --sort split on every colon and used only the first two pieces, so "@timestamp:desc,level:asc" sent order "desc,level" and a field containing a colon was cut short (#84 item 3)
divergences.toil: --sort takes comma-separated field:order pairs, each split on its last colon when asc or desc follows (case-insensitive, sent lowercase); an entry without one is all field, ascending. Each pair becomes one {field: {order}} entry in the body's sort array. The search API documents its sort parameter as "a comma-separated list of <field>:<direction> pairs": https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elasticsearch/operation/operation-search and https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/sort-search-results
divergences.why: The maintainer had this area rebuilt from Elastic's API docs (#38), and the docs give the field:direction form as a comma-separated list.

divergences.old: elasticsearch indices list failing with a raw TypeError when the server's answer wasn't a list
divergences.toil: An HTTP error saying the answer wasn't a list of indices, with a fix to check baseUrl points at Elasticsearch
divergences.why: Errors say plainly what went wrong and what to do about it.

divergences.old: elasticsearch search and count sending an empty --index, or an empty comma-separated target in --index or --pattern, to the server: an empty --index became a request to /_search or /_count, which reaches every index
divergences.toil: INVALID_INPUT before any request, naming the flag and the value; --pattern left out entirely still lists every index
divergences.why: An agent that sends an empty index would otherwise get the whole cluster back with no error.

divergences.old: elasticsearch search leaving aggregations out of the JSON when the response had none, and totalRelation out when hits.total was a bare number
divergences.toil: The same: both fields are absent in those cases. No flag asks for aggregations (--query is only the query clause), so a real search returns none; totalRelation is present whenever Elasticsearch sends hits.total as {value, relation}, as it does from 7.0
divergences.why: Not a change in behaviour. The contract lists both as always present because the old code always assigned them, but JSON drops a field whose value is undefined; the fixture keeps Elasticsearch's real response shapes rather than inventing aggregations nobody asked for.
